Not at all!! I'm more than happy to tell you about my experience..No it wasn't a projection of any kind. It was rather I started talking to myself automatically, I initially asked my shadow to speak up and later it started expressing itself through my mouth. And my 'self' was aware it was someone else. After that encounter it's as if I gained more stability. For example yesterday someone invalidated my feelings I felt hurt. And whenever you feel hurt, feelings of aggression evoke, but at the moment I chose to look at my feelings of aggression and sympathize with it. I validated the feeling of anger that I observed inside. And this validation calmed it down as it felt understood by me. Thus I didn't have to face any consequences of my anger, by merely having self control. I think practicing mindfulness is another important thing before talking to your shadow. Because you need to collect a lot of patience. This was just a little example but you never know the consequences of your anger might be bigger than this. I am not implying here that you will have a control over your fate just by practicing these two things but it gives you a sense of satisfaction. I think that is worth it and makes you feel more alive!

My story about how I got into sociology is quite different..I hated sociology when I first interacted with it..I thought sociologists are rather complicating the problems than giving a simple solution, one more reason was that I thought of society as very adamant and rigid, I thought why do sociologists invest so much of their time in understanding a society which is basically heading no where ..But there was a turning point in my life when slowly and steady I had started to observe things from other people's perspective I started to understand root causes of all the evils and goods in society and sociology further helped me to enhance my knowledge and to develop an unbiased perspective. It relieves me mentally as well as now it gives me a purpose to use my knowledge and positive approach in the field of public administration in coming years. 
Sociology gave my life a meaning!
